qti-assessment-test.title: K2 Enterprises - AI & FTC Safeguards Data Security Controls for Accounting Firms (NASBA QAS Self-Study Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply FTC Safeguards Rule and IRC Sec. 7216 controls to AI tax-prep workflows.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply FTC Safeguards Rule and IRC Sec. 7216 controls to AI tax-prep workflows.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A senior tax associate wants to summarize a client's multi-state K-1 footnotes using an external generative AI workspace. Under FTC Safeguards Rule WISP requirements and IRC Section 7216, which control sequence is required before uploading schedule excerpts?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Verify an executed zero-data-retention enterprise agreement, strip taxpayer-identifying fields, and log workpaper review.
Upload the raw K-1 PDF into a personal pro-tier chatbot account and delete the chat thread immediately afterward.
Replace the client's company name with initials while leaving EINs and partner SSNs intact for cross-referencing.
Obtain verbal permission from the engagement partner without checking vendor data-training retention terms.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Combining contractual zero-retention isolation, taxpayer identifier redaction, and documented reviewer sign-off satisfies both FTC Safeguards WISP controls and IRC Sec. 7216 disclosure boundaries.
Incorrect. Deleting a consumer chat thread after upload does not prevent provider telemetry retention or satisfy IRC Sec. 7216 prior-consent rules.
Incorrect. Leaving EINs and SSNs intact transmits direct taxpayer identifiers to an unauthorized third-party processor.
Incorrect. Internal partner sign-off cannot override statutory IRC Sec. 7216 taxpayer consent or WISP vendor due-diligence mandates.

qti-assessment-item.title: Distinguish NASBA QAS Self-Study review questions from qualified final exam items.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Distinguish NASBA QAS Self-Study review questions from qualified final exam items.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: When converting a live CPA CPE webinar transcript into an on-demand NASBA QAS Self-Study module, how must review questions differ from final examination items?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Review questions provide immediate option-level corrective rationales during instruction, while final exam items measure mastery without revealing answers pre-submission.
Review questions may consist solely of True/False prompts, whereas final exam items require untimed open-ended essays.
Review questions count for 50% of the passing CPE score, while the final exam is optional if seat time exceeds 50 minutes.
Review questions and final exam items may reuse identical verbatim stems so learners memorize key definitions.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. NASBA QAS Self-Study standards require periodic review questions with diagnostic feedback explaining why each choice is right or wrong, paired with a separate scored final exam.
Incorrect. NASBA standards restrict True/False reliance and use objective machine-gradable items mapped to learning objectives.
Incorrect. QAS Self-Study credit requires passing the scored final examination (typically >= 70%), not seat-time timers alone.
Incorrect. Verbatim stem reuse between review checkpoints and the scored final examination invalidates assessment independence.

qti-assessment-item.title: Detect fabricated authoritative citations in AI-assisted accounting research.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Detect fabricated authoritative citations in AI-assisted accounting research.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An AI research assistant drafts a lease-modification memo citing 'ASC 842-10-55-194(b)' for a sale-leaseback reassessment. What is the required audit-documentation step before filing the memo?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Retrieve the exact FASB Accounting Standards Codification paragraph directly from the authoritative database and attach the verified excerpt.
Ask the same language model in a fresh session whether ASC 842-10-55-194(b) is accurate and screenshot its confirmation.
Accept the citation if the economic conclusion matches last year's reviewed workpaper summary.
Remove all Codification citations from the memo so no specific paragraph number can be challenged during peer review.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Language models frequently synthesize plausible-looking sub-paragraph numbers; direct Codification lookup prevents citing non-existent guidance in audit workpapers.
Incorrect. Self-verification in a second LLM prompt exhibits sycophancy and shared pretraining blind spots rather than primary-source verification.
Incorrect. Prior-year conclusion alignment does not validate an unverified Codification paragraph reference in current-year workpapers.
Incorrect. Omitting authoritative support weakens technical workpaper documentation under AICPA audit quality standards.
